newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian sugar plantings expected to be down.
newsitem.headline: Belgian sugar plantings expected to be down.

text.p: Belgian sugar beet plantings are expected to be down for 1997/98, processors have told the Belgian Institute for the Improvement of Beet (IRBAB).

"The start of sowing is likely to be a little later than the usual mid-March period and sowing is likely to start at the end of the month depending on weather conditions," IRBAB's Mia Tits told Reuters on Wednesday.
She confirmed that Belgian processors had told the IRBAB they were anticipating sowings will be "about one percent down" on last year's figure of around 104,000 hectares.
The slight reduction in plantings would reflect the high sugar content of 17.16 percent of Belgian beet in 1996/97, she added.
